endorsements.quote: Establish legal frameworks, an AI registry, clear accountability, incident reporting, and postdeployment review cycles.
Implement, and monitor, education and training programs to enhance local expertise.
Provide in-workflow support and feedback loops; monitor adoption and outcomes; iterate based on user-reported issues.

unlisted_practices: Establish regional networks tailored to low-resource settings that translate high-level AI principles into feasible steps and sequence requirements according to local maturity.
Prioritize AI use cases that reflect local disease burdens and primary care needs.
Plan deployments around connectivity tiers with offline-first operation, deploy edge compute where needed, and invest in resilient power and basic data hubs.
Build representative local datasets through data partnerships, measurable data inclusion targets, and privacy-preserving methods such as federated learning.
Couple pilots to maintenance, monitoring, and clear measures of value to avoid pilotitis and ensure sustainability.
Use open standards and public-interest clauses in partnerships to reduce vendor lock-in and enable local maintenance.
Evaluate public-private partnerships carefully for risks and costs against alternatives such as domestic financing.
Align local AI solutions with existing global standards and ethically justify any divergence.
Involve local healthcare professionals actively in AI development.
Assess how traditional healing practices may affect AI predictive models and account for them.
Support open science and data sharing to prevent monopolies on clinical AI.
Establish strong, transparent data privacy regulations and cybersecurity measures for organizations handling medical data.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary proposing a framework and regional network approach for responsible AI governance, data sovereignty, and infrastructure in low-resource health systems.
